### 🪓 Survival: gather, chop, craft
- You now start survival empty-handed and build up from the ground: **sticks and stones** lie scattered on the forest floor — aim at one and pick it up with the interact key.
- **Trees and boulders can be broken down.** Swing a tool at a trunk and it falls; swing a pick at a boulder and it yields stone, or iron ore if it's one of the rust-streaked ones. The right tool matters — an axe eats wood, a pick eats rock, a knife barely scratches either, and guns do nothing at all.
- **A crafting mat** in the backpack turns what you gathered into gear: torch, knife, axe, pick, bow and arrows, 9 mm / shotgun / rifle ammo, medkits, a shield, mines and sentries — sorted into tabs by category.
- Click a recipe you can afford to lay it out, click it again to add another batch, and the gear builds them all at once. Crafting takes time (a sentry takes far longer than a torch) — but nothing leaves your backpack until it finishes, so cancelling costs you nothing.
- **Tools now come in two tiers.** The stone axe and pick are craftable the hour you land — four stones off the floor, no ore needed. Their forged versions swing the same but bite far deeper: an iron axe drops a tree in two chops. Ore comes out of boulders, so the whole early game is one line — stone tools, then ore, then iron tools.
- **Blueberry bushes** in the undergrowth can be stripped of their fruit. A handful heals a little and is eaten fast — forage food you live off between hunts. The bush stays standing, minus its berries.

### 🌦️ Weather
- **The sky has weather now** — clear days, overcast, rain, thunderstorms, snow and blizzards, and it changes as the days pass in survival.
- Fronts **roll in gradually** instead of switching on: the light dims, the wind picks up, the trees start moving, and then it starts falling.
- **Storms flash and rumble.** Lightning lights up the whole world for an instant, and thunder rolls in nearer or further away.
- Rain and snow fall around you and are stopped by roofs in the arena maps.
- In PvP and PvE lobbies the host **picks the weather for the room**; survival derives its own from the world.
- Rain/snow density is its own graphics setting, so a weaker machine can turn it down or off.

### 🌬️ A world that moves
- **The forest sways in the wind.** Treetops lean and shiver, harder as the weather turns, and their shadows move with them.

### 💧 Lakes, ponds and swimming
- The survival world has **standing water** — everything from an ankle-deep puddle to a lake big enough to swim across, each sitting in its own bowl with bays and headlands rather than a round crater.
- **You can wade and swim.** Water drags on you as it gets deeper, and past waist height you start swimming and floating. There's an underwater view when you go under.
- **Water sounds like water**: the splash of breaking the surface (bigger the harder you drop in), a stroke per arm-pull while swimming, and the water on your boots as you wade — layered over the footstep, not instead of it.

### 🌿 A world with more in it
- **Undergrowth**: bushes, blueberry bushes, ferns, saplings and dead scrub fill the layer between the grass and the treetops. All of it is walk-through.
- **Boulders** are back in the landscape as the world's source of stone, with rarer ore-bearing ones as the only metal.
- Reworked terrain, biomes, grass and ground shading throughout.

### 🧟 Zombies that have to notice you first
- In survival, zombies now **spawn unaware** and shamble around where they were, until you come close enough — or shoot one. Lose them long enough and they settle back down.
- Zombies come out at night in growing numbers; the horde waves in the PvE modes are unchanged and still come straight for you.
- **Zombies are much tougher to put down with body shots — and just as easy with headshots.** A hit to the skull crits, whether it's a bullet or an axe, so a horde now punishes sloppy aim instead of soaking ammo either way.
- **Spiders** — neutral, they scuttle around their nest, rear up when you approach, and if you get too close they land a venomous bite and dart away.
- Wildlife no longer materialises in plain sight a short walk away — animals fade in at the same distance zombies do.

### 🤝 Wandering traders
- A **friendly trader** occasionally shows up in the survival world and appears on your minimap. There's no money — he barters gear for the materials you've been gathering, and better guns ask for scarcer loot. He also stocks forged tools, which is a real find on a world with no ore nearby.
- **You open a deal by looking at him**, not by walking past him — so brushing by a trader on your way somewhere no longer offers you a trade.
- Mobs now **drop loot** when killed: cloth, bone, scrap metal, rotten flesh, leather, and raw meat off wildlife.
- Food and medkits are used **from your hands**, with their own animation — no more healing with a click through an open backpack.

### 🔊 Sound
- **Felling a tree sounds like it**: the trunk tears off the stump as it starts to go, and the canopy lands a second later — audible right across the valley, so you hear someone else working in co-op. Boulders come apart into scree.
- **Crafting is audible** — the work goes on for as long as the job takes, and you hear the piece being set down and finished.
- Chopping wood and breaking rock no longer repeat one identical thud — every blow lands a little differently.
- Footsteps in grass were toned down; it's the sound you hear most in the game and it was sitting over everything else.

### 💾 Saved worlds
- **Survival worlds now save themselves.** The lobby has a "Continue" list: your landscape, position, gear, time of day and difficulty come back exactly as you left them.
- Each save shows the day you reached, how long you've played and when you last touched it. Worlds can be deleted from the same list.
- Joining someone else's world plays in their landscape — it doesn't land in your own save list.
- Dying no longer overwrites your world: quitting from the death screen keeps the last living snapshot.
- If your browser refuses to store the world (full storage, private mode), **the game now tells you** instead of quietly stopping to save.

### 🗺️ Minimap
- The minimap now draws the actual world under you — terrain, biomes and the water sitting in them.

### 🏃 Arcade movement
- A new arcade movement profile: snappy acceleration, real air-strafing, and bunny-hopping that chains instead of bleeding speed on every landing.
- Sliding.
- Movement physics now step at a fixed 120 Hz, so how you move no longer depends on your frame rate.
- Field of view is a fixed 90° in every movement profile.
- Stepping up onto a ledge eases the view instead of snapping it.

### 🌐 Multiplayer
- Other players move more smoothly, especially on an unstable connection — their motion is now replayed on the sender's clock rather than on whenever the packet happened to arrive.

### ✨ Visuals
- **Ambient occlusion (SSAO)** — soft shading settles into corners and under objects. It's a graphics setting, so you can turn it off.
- Weapons picked up depth: seams, magazine wells, trigger guards and the gaps under scopes are now shaded instead of reading as flat blocks of colour.
- The sky now lights the world — weapons, players and props take their ambient light and reflections from the actual sky above you, so they shift with the time of day.
